readings.title: Rain on opposite sides of town
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Two volunteer weather groups reported different rainfall totals after the same storm. Some residents assumed one group had made a mistake. The coordinators compared the locations and discovered that the gauges were several kilometres apart. Both had been installed properly, and the storm had passed more heavily over the western district. The groups published a map with their readings instead of producing a single average. They also explained how measurements were taken. Differences were therefore presented as useful information about the storm, while equipment checks remained part of the routine.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A warning people could use
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A village notice warned residents of a strong wind but gave no advice about the outdoor market scheduled for that afternoon. Traders kept calling the office to ask whether they should travel. The organiser added a clear decision time and explained where the final announcement would appear. She also described the sheltered alternative location. The revised notice did not make the forecast more certain, but it reduced confusion about what would happen next. Residents could distinguish the uncertain weather from the definite process for making a decision. The office adopted the same approach for later public events.

readings.title: Shade and the thermometer
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A school club wanted to compare temperatures in its courtyard and garden. One pupil placed a thermometer in direct sunlight because the courtyard felt hot. Another put a device under a tree. Their first comparison mixed two questions: how warm the air was and how much sunlight heated the instruments. With guidance, they placed matching thermometers in shaded, ventilated covers at the same height. The courtyard still recorded higher afternoon temperatures on several days. The club described its method and avoided claiming that the results represented every season. Improving the comparison made its limited conclusion more useful.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Reading the old weather diary
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An archive volunteer found a gardener's diary containing descriptions of frost, flowering trees and muddy paths. It was tempting to turn every entry into a precise temperature estimate. An experienced researcher warned that words such as 'cold' depended on the writer's experience. The diary was still valuable when combined with dated photographs and other records. It could show when particular plants flowered and how weather affected daily work. The archive therefore kept the original wording and added notes explaining uncertainty. Preserving a record did not require pretending it answered questions it had never been designed to answer.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Weather information is most useful when people understand its limits. A forecast describes what is likely to happen, not what is certain to happen. Local observations can add valuable detail, but a single unusual day does not establish a long-term pattern. Careful records make comparisons more meaningful.
translation.referenceAnswer: 天气信息在人们理解其局限时最为有用。天气预报描述的是可能发生的情况，而不是必然发生的情况。当地观测能补充有价值的细节，但某一天的异常情况并不能证明长期规律。细致的记录能使比较更有意义。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

criteria.description: 准确传达各句核心信息、对象和逻辑关系；按遗漏或误译程度酌情扣分。

criteria.description: 中文自然通顺，句间衔接合理；不拘泥于英语词序。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss why local weather records can be useful. Suggest how volunteers can collect and communicate observations responsibly.
writing.sampleAnswer: Local weather records can help a community understand differences between nearby areas and plan outdoor activities. For example, rainfall recorded near a garden may explain why its soil is wetter than expected. Volunteers should use suitable equipment, follow the same method and note the location and time of each observation. They should also record unusual conditions that might affect a reading. When sharing results, the group must distinguish observations from predictions. A wet week does not by itself prove a long-term change. A simple chart with dates and a short explanation would be useful. Keeping original records and correcting mistakes openly would make the project more trustworthy. Careful local work can contribute useful detail without claiming to answer every weather question.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
